steps.text: Place stewed tomatoes, 3 cups water, beef broth, lima beans, corn, sliced carrots, chopped onion, and Old Bay seasoning in a 4-quart pot. Bring to a simmer over medium heat; cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Bring 1 gallon water to a boil in a large pot. Add crab claws and boil for 6 minutes; drain.
Stir crabmeat and boiled crab claws into tomato and vegetable mixture. Cover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes. Serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Maryland Crab Soup
raw_recipe.description: This crab soup recipe is authentic Chesapeake Bay food made with Old Bay, lima beans, corn, carrots, and Maryland blue back-fin crab meat and claws.
raw_recipe.name: Maryland Crab Soup

recipeInstructions.text: Place stewed tomatoes, 3 cups water, beef broth, lima beans, corn, sliced carrots, chopped onion, and Old Bay seasoning in a 4-quart pot. Bring to a simmer over medium heat; cover and cook for 5 minutes.
Bring 1 gallon water to a boil in a large pot. Add crab claws and boil for 6 minutes; drain.
Stir crabmeat and boiled crab claws into tomato and vegetable mixture. Cover and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes. Serve hot.

review.reviewBody: This is a wonderful recipe for crab soup. I am from MD and can get this in restaurants but have been looking for a recipe like this for a long time. I do add some extra things, like chopped cabbage, potatoes, and birds eye frozen mixed vegs. I don't like lima beans so I leave them out. The extra veggies make the soup take longer to cook but it is really DELICIOUS! **Try not to use pasteurized or canned crab meat or it will give the soup a "fishy" taste. Fresh crab meat works the best (if you can find it in your area).

I am also from Maryland and although I made a number of adjustments, this is a very good basic recipe. Here is what changed: I used crushed tomatoes instead of stewed (28 oz can), used Birdseye frozen veggies, which has green beans, corn and peas (2 small bags), 1 1/2 cups cubed potatoes, 1/2 cup chopped savoy cabbage, 2 cans (not cups) of beef broth (low sodium), 1/4 cup brown sugar and 1 T. Worcheshire sauce. 3 Tablespoons of Old Bay was perfect for me, but for someone who isn't from the area, it might be a little too spicy. I cooked it much longer on low (about 2 hours), but I don't serve it until the next day so all of the flavors can develop.

I live in western PA. no fresh blue crab in my neighborhood. i did however have a package of imitation crab meat. I know all you marylanders are kringing lol. I made the recipe pretty much as written with that exception and a couple of others . I only had 1 can of stewed tomatoes so I used that and 1 can of diced and I had a can of Delallo's red clam sauce so I added that. {a little olive oil , garlic and basil never hurt anyone } It was great and I made a crab salad with peas and bacon with the other half of the package of "crabby meat". also great. I didn't have limas so added potatoes. I thought edamame would be a good substitute too.

I did make a few little changes to this recipe. I sauteed carrots onions and celery before I added the stewed tomatoes and the broth and I feel that made a big difference to the recipe. As well as adding more Old Bay seasoning. I'm in Idaho so I don't have access to blue crab so I made the most of it and used pasteurized claw meat and lump crab meat and it turned out pretty well. I gave some to my friends and they loved it and they're from the back east

This is an excellent recipe. I sauteed onion and green pepper in a little butter/magarine first then added the other ingredients. I also used more seasonings for the flavor (garlic, oregano, bay leaves, creole seasoning, salt, pepper, and old bay). About a tablespoon of worchester sauce and 2 teaspoons of brown sugar. Yum Yum!
I used 1 can of fire roasted tomatoes and 1 can stewed tomatoes. I left out the lima beans and added green beans and peas instead. I made it very veggie heavy. Everyone loved it!

This is a real deal for good crab soup and that is coming from someone in Baltimore who has made crab soup from scratch!
I did crush and cook the tomatoes, Old Bay and onions separately for 15 mins before adding the vegetables and then the crab meat. Cooking for another 15.
Next time, think I'll add a bay leaf and 1-2 tablespoons of Worcestershire Sauce to add some more depth to the broth.
If you want to "bump up" the crab taste you can throw the uncooked crab claws into the soup to cook as opposed to cooking them separately. That's how cooks do it in Maryland when cooking crab soup from scratch.

Great recipe, everybody liked it. I made it a few times. The second time I changed a few things and it came out the best. I omitted the Lima beans (both me and the wife didn't think they went with this soup. I added cube potatoes, 2 tbs of brown sugar, a dash of Worcestershire sauce, two stalks of celery diced up and one bay leaf and 3 tablespoons of old bay (we like everything spicy). I also only used beef stock and no water, crush tomatoes instead of stewed tomatoes and 1 tea spoon of tomato paste (if you don't have no biggie). At the end of cooking I added two tablespoons of sherry, again if you don't have no biggie but it does go really well with this soup. Just a hint, if you use celery in anything use you peeler on it first, it helps to keep it from not to getting stringy.

Gives a good base so you can make it your own. So as a native of Southern Maryland I had to change it up a bit. I cut the water in half (or you wouldn't be able to find the crab meat). Added 2 cans of tomato soup, 3 diced white potatoes, 1/2 tsp sugar, salt and pepper, ground cayenne pepper, about a tbsp of Franks's hot sauce and more old bay (we like spicy). BTW next time I will go with the diced tomatoes since I cut the stewed in cubes.

I’ve used this recipe many different ways. I prefer using a 28 oz can of crushed tomatoes and using a frozen veg blend (corn, carrots, Lima’s, green beans) added toward the end. Also,taste your broth and adjust seasonings as needed. Although crazy for a true Marylander, I found a bit of brown sugar balanced the acidity of the tomatoes.

This is a very good and authentic recipe, as is for sure. I tend to adjust things to personal taste, and like to use as many on-hand ingredients as possible, so I used more Old Bay seasoning and flageolet beans instead of the limas (flageolet beans are also light green, but shaped more like cannellini, have characteristics of both lima and cannellini about them). I also used organic bone broth (chicken) instead of water, for more protein and a little added flavor. It was great.

I think adding crabs in shell to the process (as suggested as optional) would add a good dimension to the soup, but didn't have the full crab (I used 1 lb of lump crab meat from Costco).
Pretty good base for starters. I added precooked new potatoes water drained and cut into a diced cut as well as added Thyme and Saffron into the mixture. Great recipe overall.

Wonderful. I don't like Lima beans, so I substituted peas. Yesterday my daughter treated me to a crab feast, so I had left over a lot of claws and 3 or 4 crabs which I picked and included along with the can of crab flaw from the grocery store. Extra old Bay since I live in Baltimore, and it came out very well. 5 stars. Edit: after having about 5 bowls myself and sharing it with other family members, it was a big hit. Excellanté
Loved everything about this I added the claws but also legs and clusters

Always in search of a good crab soup recipe, I made this last weekend. I had steamed crab claws in the freezer from our crab night during the holidays and this was a good way to use those up. And the seasoned claws added some extra old bay flavor. I added some chopped cabbage and a can of diced potatoes as these are the traditions in our part of Maryland's eastern shore. Overall we really enjoyed this with my tweaks. I will definitely keep this recipe. I think it would make a great extra dish for our next crab feast! p.a. I also appreciated not having to deal with a ham hock or bone!!
I make a stock or soup base using smoked hocks. Also use some cabbage to cut the acidity of the tomatoes. Eastern shore Maryland.
Fresh vegetables help, also fresh green beans are easier to get than Limas, so,Acceptable substitute . I like to throw a couple or three potatoes. Helps fill you up/ make the soup last another day.

So glad I ran across this recipe. I've always been a big fan of cream of crab soup, but not so much MD crab soup because I don't like most vegetables in it. It never occurred to me to just leave them out and this recipe has nothing in it that I don't like. As an added bonus, it's so much healthier than cream of crab. The only deviations I made were unintentional; I had to use pasteurized lump crabmeat because I couldn't get my hands on any fresh jumbo lump (and I live in the Chesapeake Bay region of MD!) and based on suggestions from other reviews I was going to put cabbage in it but I completely forgot. Also, I used one can of regular stewed tomatoes and one can of Italian seasoned tomatoes and I did wind up taking them out of the pot to cut them up some then re-added them back in. None of these changes mattered though because this soup turned out delicious! I shared it with my 95 year old stepdad who is a crab soup connoisseur and brutally honest about my cooking and he said it was as good as, if not better than, any crab soup he has ever had. The next time I eat crabs I'm going to pick some meat to put aside to make this recipe again and I will add some claws and cabbage. Kudos to the originator of this recipe!!
